Constitution

1. Name and Registered Office

Article 1 – The association’s name is “Çalışma Hayatı ve Sosyal Politika Araştırmaları Derneği” (Working Life and Social Policy Research Association). Its registered office is in Ankara. Its abbreviated name is “ÇAHSPAR”. The association may establish branches in Türkiye and abroad.

2. Purpose, Activities and Scope

Article 2 – The association was established to improve the quality of working and social life through innovative, sustainable, not-for-profit research, training, projects and consultancy in working life and social policy.

Within this scope, the association aims to develop sustainable solutions in decent work, social protection, employment, gender equality, environmental awareness and social policy.

The association’s activities and methods are as follows:

  • Undertake training, research, public opinion research, projects and academic studies nationally and internationally.
  • Organise and deliver all forms of certified training, including courses, seminars, conferences, panels and information sessions.
  • Collaborate with national and international institutions and organisations and establish research and project platforms.
  • Join and obtain accreditation from national and international umbrella organisations established for purposes consistent with its own, and accredit national associations.
  • Obtain necessary information, records, documents and publications; establish a documentation centre; and provide information and publications on employment, working life and social policy.
  • Publish an academic journal and support scholarly work.
  • Organise academic events such as congresses, workshops and conferences.
  • Establish foundations, federations and institutes where necessary.
  • Provide a healthy working environment and manage matters relating to necessary technical tools, equipment and property.
  • Establish funds and similar assistance mechanisms to meet members’ basic needs.
  • Undertake fundraising with the necessary permission, and accept donations and voluntary services.
  • Establish and make available club premises and social and cultural facilities for members.
  • Organise meetings, concerts, exhibitions, sports, trips and recreational activities to develop social relationships among members.
  • Establish branches and representative offices where necessary.

The association’s scope covers all forms of training, research, consultancy and project activities relating to working life and social policy in Türkiye and abroad.

3. Eligibility for Membership and Membership Procedures

Article 3 – Anyone who meets the conditions specified in the Law on Associations, accepts the association’s purposes and principles and agrees to work towards them may apply for membership.

The association has the following membership categories:

  • Full membership
  • Honorary membership
  • Membership of honour

Full membership: Academics, researchers, specialists, employers, natural persons and legal entities with legal capacity who accept the association’s purposes and principles and meet the statutory conditions are entitled to become members.

Honorary membership: By decision of the Board of Directors, honorary membership may be granted to people who show a close interest in the association, have undertaken significant work or have contributed to fields related to its purpose.

Membership of honour: People who have made significant material and non-material contributions to the association may be admitted as members of honour by decision of the Board of Directors.

Article 4 – Applications submitted to the association’s chair shall be accepted or rejected by the Board of Directors within thirty days at the latest. Applicants shall be informed of the outcome in writing.

The association’s full members consist of its founders and those admitted by decision of the Board of Directors following an application.

4. Members’ Rights and Duties

Article 5 – Members have equal rights. Each member has one vote at the General Assembly. Honorary members do not have voting rights.

Members shall pay the admission fee and monthly or annual subscriptions determined by the General Assembly.

5. Resignation, Expulsion and Termination of Membership

Article 6 – Every member has the right to resign by written notice. Resignation is considered complete when the notice reaches the Board of Directors.

Article 7 – The following constitute grounds for expulsion:

  • Acting contrary to the association’s constitution
  • Persistently avoiding assigned duties
  • Failing to pay subscriptions within six months despite a warning
  • Failing to comply with decisions of the association’s governing bodies
  • No longer meeting the conditions for membership
  • Prolonged inactivity due to ill health, old age, detention or similar reasons

Where any of these circumstances is established, the member shall be expelled by decision of the Board of Directors.

Article 8 – Membership terminates automatically in the following circumstances:

  • The member’s death
  • The member’s resignation
  • Loss of the capacity to exercise civil rights
  • The emergence of a legal impediment to membership or loss of the required qualifications

6. Governing Bodies

Article 9 – The association’s governing bodies are:

  • The General Assembly
  • The Board of Directors
  • The Supervisory Board

7. General Assembly

Article 10 – The General Assembly is the association’s highest decision-making body. It consists of registered members and, where applicable, branch or representative office delegates and elected delegates.

The General Assembly holds ordinary and extraordinary meetings.

The ordinary General Assembly meets every three years in June. An extraordinary General Assembly is convened when deemed necessary by the Board of Directors or Supervisory Board, or upon the written request of one fifth of members.

Members entitled to attend shall be invited at least fifteen days before the meeting. The date, time, venue and agenda shall be announced appropriately. If the first meeting does not achieve a quorum, a second meeting may be held.

The General Assembly requires an absolute majority of members entitled to attend; a two-thirds majority is required for constitutional amendments and dissolution.

Each member has one vote at the General Assembly and must vote in person. Legal entities vote through a representative.

8. Duties and Powers of the General Assembly

Article 11 – The General Assembly’s duties and powers are:

  • Electing the association’s governing bodies
  • Amending the constitution
  • Discussing reports of the Board of Directors and Supervisory Board
  • Approving the budget
  • Supervising governing bodies and removing them from office where necessary
  • Approving property purchases, sales and similar significant decisions
  • Deciding on admission to and expulsion from membership
  • Deciding on joining or leaving a federation
  • Authorising the opening and closure of branches and representative offices
  • Deciding on dissolution and liquidation

9. Board of Directors

Article 12 – The Board of Directors is elected by the General Assembly and consists of five principal and five substitute members.

At its first meeting, the Board allocates responsibilities and appoints a chair, deputy chair, general secretary, treasurer and accounting officer.

The Board is the association’s executive body. It represents the association in its affairs, takes decisions and implements them.

Its duties include:

  • Carrying out tasks assigned by the General Assembly
  • Representing the association or delegating authority to one or more members
  • Managing income and expenditure accounts
  • Preparing the budget for the following period and submitting it to the General Assembly
  • Preparing regulations governing the association’s work
  • Managing property purchases and sales, leases, pledges and similar transactions
  • Undertaking procedures to establish branches and representative offices
  • Preparing activity reports
  • Deciding on membership applications, rejections and expulsions

10. Supervisory Board

Article 13 – The Supervisory Board is elected by the General Assembly and consists of three principal and three substitute members.

It examines whether the association’s activities, books and accounts comply with legislation and the constitution. It reports its findings to the Board of Directors and, where necessary, the General Assembly.

11. Sources of Income

Article 14 – The association’s income sources are:

  • Membership subscriptions
  • Branch contributions
  • Donations and assistance from natural persons and legal entities
  • Income from tea gatherings, dinners, trips, concerts, competitions, congresses, workshops, conferences and similar events
  • Income from academic publications and publishing
  • Income from the association’s assets
  • Fundraising conducted in accordance with legislation
  • Profits from commercial activities
  • Profits from the academic journal
  • Other income

12. Bookkeeping Principles and Procedures

Article 15 – The association shall keep its books on the operating account basis. If its annual gross income exceeds the specified threshold, it shall adopt the balance sheet basis.

Books and records shall be maintained in accordance with the Regulation on Associations.

The books to be kept include:

  • Membership Register
  • Decision Book
  • Correspondence Registers
  • Balance Sheet, Budget and Final Accounts Book
  • Income and Expenditure Book
  • Fixed Asset Register
  • Receipt Register

13. Income and Expenditure Procedures

Article 16 – Income shall be collected against a receipt. For income collected through a bank, the bank receipt may serve in its place.

Expenditure shall be supported by invoices, till receipts, receipts and similar expenditure documents. Expense vouchers and bank receipts may be used where necessary.

14. Declaration and Notification Obligations

Article 17 – The association’s activities and income and expenditure transactions for the preceding year shall be declared by the chair to the local administrative authority within the first four months of each calendar year.

Where required, the association shall submit notifications of General Assembly results, property holdings, assistance received from abroad, projects and changes in accordance with legislation.

15. Internal Audit

Article 18 – Internal audits may be undertaken by the General Assembly, Board of Directors or Supervisory Board. Independent audit organisations may be engaged where necessary.

The Supervisory Board shall audit the association at least once a year and report its findings.

16. Establishing Representative Offices

Article 19 – The association may establish representative offices where necessary, with authorisation from the General Assembly and a decision of the Board of Directors. Details of the representative and address shall be notified in writing to the local administrative authority.

17. Branches

Article 20 – The association may establish branches where necessary by decision of the General Assembly. Branches undertake autonomous activities in line with the association’s purposes and services.

The governing bodies of branches are:

  • The General Assembly
  • The Board of Directors
  • The Supervisory Board

18. Borrowing Procedures

Article 21 – The association may borrow by decision of the Board of Directors where necessary to achieve its purpose and carry out its activities. Borrowing must remain within the association’s income capacity and must not create payment difficulties.

19. Amending the Constitution

Article 22 – The constitution may be amended by decision of the General Assembly. Amendments require the applicable attendance and voting majorities at the General Assembly.

20. Dissolution and Liquidation of Assets

Article 23 – The General Assembly may decide to dissolve the association.

The required majority must be achieved for dissolution. Upon dissolution, a liquidation committee consisting of the last members of the Board of Directors shall liquidate the association’s funds, property and rights. Remaining assets shall be transferred to the body designated by the General Assembly or, if none is designated, to the association with the closest purpose.

The full constitution is structured within this framework in respect of the association’s institutional structure, purposes, governance model, membership arrangements and operating principles.
